note: C07.1 retrieval evaluation set (docs/policy-rag.md:29: 40 条查询，20dev/20 冻结test，按语义家族分离).
**How the split is separated, and why it is by merchant rather than by version.** The first version of this
set split dev/test by policy version (dev = the 2026.08 bundles, test = 2026.09) and the evaluation's own
split check reported four families present in both halves — correctly, because the two versions of a policy
repeat the same families: 2026.09 is 2026.08's successor, so `lost` and `signed` exist in both. That is not
a separation, and the check said so rather than being loosened to accept it.
So the split is by **policy set**, which is the dimension the corpus actually has two of:
* `dev`  — the LOGISTICS family (`policy-logistics-2026.08`), 4 semantic families;
* `test` — the DAMAGE family (`policy-damage-2026.09`), 6 families, none of which appear in dev.
Every query is still pinned to a real bundle and manifest hash, so the version filter is exercised by both
halves (dev is pinned to an August manifest, test to a September one). A consequence worth stating plainly:
**test is frozen in the sense that it was written from the damage policy and never edited after a run** — it
was authored for this corpus, not held back from an earlier experiment, because no earlier retrieval
experiment existed. It is not a held-out set of a model that was tuned on dev; nothing was tuned.
`gold` is the rule that answers the query, written as `<bundle_id>/<rule_id>`, and it was written by reading
the policy before any retrieval ran. Where two rules could both be defended the query was rewritten to be
unambiguous or dropped — a gold set adjusted to fit a ranking measures the ranking's agreement with itself.
`family` is the semantic family, and `_near_miss` marks a query whose correct answer is the
*opposite-looking* rule ("客户说没收到" must reach the signed-for rule, not the lost one) — where a
bag-of-words ranking is expected to struggle, and where BM25 beating dense is a real possibility the report
has to be willing to state.
